titles.packetOps: Construct. Read. Change. Keep the cause.
titles.failure: Failure takes time to become knowledge.

summaries.tcp: Every packet is constructed, sent, received, and processed separately. Connection state survives the exchange.
summaries.packet: Measured fields open from the compact source frame. Version, protocol, and exact byte ranges remain explicit.
summaries.packetOps: Separate envelopes touch without merging. Construction changes derive lengths and checksums from real source bytes.
summaries.failure: The physical break, control propagation, route installation, and application recovery remain separate source events.
summaries.dns: Questions, referrals, answers, and retained cache state follow the source sequence.
summaries.tls: Parameters enter the transcript, keys activate, and application data becomes opaque. Cryptographic values are symbolic.
summaries.http: TCP’s sequence hole blocks delivery across streams. QUIC’s Stream B continues while Stream A waits; congestion still affects the connection.
summaries.journey: The event sequence changes scale while retaining its request context and existing source boundaries.
summaries.provider: Underlay forwarding, the inner packet, added envelopes, and MTU outcomes remain distinguishable.
